description: Backend AWS Lambda handlers (TypeScript) for the API: save/load monster to DynamoDB and chat via Amazon Bedrock with model selection by growth stage. Handlers import pure logic from @ddm/shared. Written to compile with aws-sdk v3 + @types/aws-lambda once installed; depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create packages/backend/package.json (name @ddm/backend, type module, deps: @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb, @aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @ddm/shared workspace:*; devDeps: @types/aws-lambda, @types/node, typescript; script build=tsc).
Create packages/backend/tsconfig.json extending root base, outDir dist, rootDir src, module NodeNext.
Create packages/backend/src/dynamo.ts: DynamoDBDocumentClient setup reading TABLE_NAME from env; getMonster(id), putMonster(monster) functions.

Create packages/backend/src/handlers/getMonster.ts: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2. Reads monsterId from path/query. If none exists, returns 404 (frontend will create). On load, apply applyTimePassage + evolveStage from shared, persist if changed, return monster JSON. Include CORS headers.
Create packages/backend/src/handlers/saveMonster.ts: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2. Validates body (id, name, stats...), writes to DynamoDB via putMonster, returns saved monster. CORS headers.

Create packages/backend/src/handlers/chat.ts: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2. Body {monsterId, message}. Loads monster, determines stage; if stage.canChat is false (baby) return a canned non-verbal response (e.g. '…！' with a note that this stage cannot talk). Otherwise resolve Bedrock model id via resolveModelId(stage.bedrockModelKey, env overrides) and call BedrockRuntime InvokeModel with the Anthropic Messages API payload, injecting a system prompt that reflects the monster personality + stage. Return the assistant text. Handle errors with 502 and a friendly message. CORS headers.

Create packages/backend/src/handlers/battle.ts: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2. Body {monsterId}. Loads monster, generates a simple enemy scaled to stage, calls simulateBattle from shared, applies win/loss stat changes, persists, returns BattleResult + updated monster. CORS headers.
Create packages/backend/src/lib/http.ts: shared helpers for JSON responses + CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin configurable via env, default '*').
Add a lightweight env config module packages/backend/src/config.ts reading TABLE_NAME, ALLOWED_ORIGIN, and optional BEDROCK_MODEL_HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS overrides and AWS_REGION.
acceptance_criteria: Handler files reference @ddm/shared pure functions (evolveStage, applyTimePassage, simulateBattle, resolveModelId) rather than reimplementing logic
chat handler selects Bedrock model by stage: baby=no chat, rookie=haiku, champion=sonnet, ultimate=opus

All .ts files are syntactically valid TypeScript (env -u NODE_OPTIONS tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck on handler files parses without syntax errors; type errors from missing node_modules are expected and acceptable in-sandbox)
package.json and tsconfig.json are valid JSON
verification: env -u NODE_OPTIONS tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --moduleResolution bundler --target ES2022 packages/backend/src/**/*.ts 2>&1 | grep -v "Cannot find module" | grep -v "@aws-sdk" | (! grep -iE 'error TS1[0-9]{3}')  # ensure NO syntax (TS1xxx) errors; missing-module type errors are expected
node -e "require('fs')" validation that all package.json files parse
findings:
Backend @ddm/backend package created under packages/backend. All handlers import pure logic from @ddm/shared via the package name (NOT relative paths) so esbuild/tsc resolves through the workspace symlink after npm install. Backend's own relative imports use explicit .ts extensions (consistent with tsconfig.base rewriteRelativeImportExtensions + allowImportingTsExtensions). type-only imports use 'import type' (verbatimModuleSyntax).

FILES + EXPORTED HANDLER SYMBOLS (for FEAT-004 CDK NodejsFunction entry/handler wiring; every handler is exported as the named symbol `handler`):
- packages/backend/src/handlers/getMonster.ts  -> export const handler  (GET  /monster/{monsterId} ; also accepts ?monsterId= / ?id= / path {id})
- packages/backend/src/handlers/saveMonster.ts -> export const handler  (PUT or POST /monster ; accepts bare Monster or {monster} envelope)
- packages/backend/src/handlers/chat.ts        -> export const handler  (POST /chat ; body {monsterId, message})
- packages/backend/src/handlers/battle.ts      -> export const handler  (POST /battle ; body {monsterId, seed?})
packages/backend/src/index.ts also re-exports them as getMonsterHandler/saveMonsterHandler/chatHandler/battleHandler if a barrel entry is preferred.

HANDLER SIGNATURE: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2 (HTTP API v2 event shape). Each handler calls handlePreflight(event.requestContext?.http?.method) first and returns 204 for OPTIONS. CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin comes from env ALLOWED_ORIGIN (default '*'). So API Gateway can rely on the Lambda's own CORS headers, or configure HTTP API CORS separately.

ENV VARS NEEDED PER LAMBDA (wire via CDK):
- ALL four: TABLE_NAME (required; DynamoDB table, partition key `id`), ALLOWED_ORIGIN (optional, default '*'). AWS_REGION is auto-set by Lambda; config.ts falls back to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION then 'us-east-1'.
- chat.ts ADDITIONALLY: optional BEDROCK_MODEL_HAIKU / BEDROCK_MODEL_SONNET / BEDROCK_MODEL_OPUS overrides (fall back to @ddm/shared defaults).

IAM PERMISSIONS NEEDED PER LAMBDA:
- getMonster: dynamodb:GetItem + dynamodb:PutItem (persists after applyTimePassage/evolveStage if changed).
- saveMonster: dynamodb:PutItem.
- battle: dynamodb:GetItem + dynamodb:PutItem.
- chat: dynamodb:GetItem + bedrock:InvokeModel. Baby stage returns a canned non-verbal reply WITHOUT calling Bedrock, so even baby-only usage still only needs GetItem; grant bedrock:InvokeModel on the Claude model resources (haiku/sonnet/opus; account must have Bedrock model access enabled - document in README).

DYNAMO: packages/backend/src/dynamo.ts uses DynamoDBDocumentClient (lib-dynamodb) with marshallOptions.removeUndefinedValues=true; table key is {id}. getMonster(id)->Monster|null, putMonster(monster)->Monster. Table partition key MUST be `id` (string).

BEDROCK CALL: chat.ts uses @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime InvokeModelCommand with Anthropic Messages API body {anthropic_version:'bedrock-2023-05-31', max_tokens:300, system:<JP personality+stage prompt>, messages:[{role:'user',content:message}]}; parses response.content[].text; 502 on error. Model id resolved via resolveModelId(stage.bedrockModelKey, env overrides). Stage->model: baby=none(no chat), rookie=haiku, champion=sonnet, ultimate=opus.

VERIFICATION RUN: JSON files parse OK. 'env -u NODE_OPTIONS tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler --target ES2022 --strict --verbatimModuleSyntax --allowImportingTsExtensions' over all backend src -> only expected TS2307 (missing @ddm/shared, @aws-sdk/*, aws-lambda), TS2580 (process/Buffer need @types/node), TS7006 (event implicitly any because APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2 unresolved). ZERO TS1xxx syntax errors (explicit grep gate passed). Shared tests still 22 pass / 0 fail. All resolve once user runs npm install. No commit made; changes left in working tree.
